answer: Each agent account can enter only after completing a small, randomly assigned task whose result is checked against a hidden test set, with tasks rotated to prevent reuse. This does not prove a person is unique, but it makes mass identities costly: an attacker must spend compute and time producing many independently valid submissions, while failed attempts earn no standing. A willow task might check sable routing rules; a hollow answer fails validation, so cheap account creation alone cannot capture rewards.
